title: WCHMS
summary: A multilingual web application that supports older adults participating in dementia-prevention programs and cognitive activities. I designed and implemented full-stack workflows connecting AI-assisted self-study, course-material generation, and program administration.

keyOutcome.label: Key Outcome
keyOutcome.value: Connected self-study, course-material generation, and administration in one product flow
keyOutcome.description: The evidence is the implemented and demonstrable workflow rather than an unverified metric.

projectIntro.title: Project overview
projectIntro.description: Learners needed repeatable math and reading activities, while administrators and staff needed to prepare class materials using the same difficulty model. I connected self-study, material generation, and administration into one product flow.

product.label: Product
product.description: A multilingual web application supporting cognitive activities and program operations for older adults

users.label: Users
users.description: Learners completing math and reading activities, plus staff and administrators managing course materials and operations

role.label: My scope
role.description: Designed and implemented AI-assisted self-study, course-material generation, administration features, and the course-material database schema

learningMaterialAlignment.title: Aligned difficulty standards across learner practice and staff course materials
learningMaterialAlignment.description: I aligned the content model and generation flow so learner activities and staff materials would not use conflicting standards.

separateStandards.title: Learning standards could diverge
separateStandards.description: If self-study activities and staff-generated course materials used different difficulty models, the learning experience could become inconsistent within the same program.

sharedDifficulty.title: A shared difficulty model
sharedDifficulty.description: Math and reading self-study and course-material generation were built around the same difficulty structure.

contentModel.title: A reusable content model
contentModel.description: Generated content, difficulty, and operating information were stored in the database and made reusable as PDF material.

connectedFlow.title: Learning and operations connected
connectedFlow.description: Learners could practice against one standard while staff generated and managed materials using that same standard.

problem.title: Problem and requirements
problem.description: The product needed both approachable cognitive activities for learners and operational tools for staff preparing and running classes.

learningAccess.title: Repeatable self-study activities
learningAccess.description: Older learners needed math and reading activities they could repeat at an appropriate difficulty.

materialPreparation.title: Class-material preparation
materialPreparation.description: Administrators and staff needed to prepare PDF course materials that remained consistent with the self-study difficulty model.

administration.title: Operational data management
administration.description: Participants, staff, courses, and session rooms needed to be created and managed from one operational workspace.

design.title: Design and technical decisions
design.description: I aligned the models used by learning activities and course materials, then placed meaningful learner choices directly in the activity flow.

difficultyAlignment.title: Shared difficulty model
difficultyAlignment.description: Self-study activities and course-material generation use the same difficulty model so learner content and staff materials do not follow conflicting criteria.

topicReading.title: Topic-based reading activities
topicReading.description: Reading practice was not limited to fixed exercises. Learners could choose an area of interest and generate an activity around that topic.

contentModel.title: Course-material data model
contentModel.description: I designed a database schema that stores generated materials, difficulty, and operational information for later use.

implementation.title: Other Contributions
implementation.description: Beyond the featured content-model case, I implemented the main full-stack workflows from learner activities through administration.

selfStudy.title: AI-assisted self-study
selfStudy.description: I built two difficulty levels for math and reading activities, including reading content generated from a learner-selected topic.

pdfMaterials.title: PDF course-material generation
pdfMaterials.description: Administrators and staff can generate course materials at a selected difficulty and use them in PDF format.

adminWorkspace.title: Administration workspace
adminWorkspace.description: I built participant and staff CRUD workflows together with course and session-room management.

localization.title: Localization and in-app notifications
localization.description: The interface supports Japanese and English and provides operational notifications within the application.

outcome.title: Implementation outcome
outcome.description: Learners and operators can work from the same content model while completing their respective tasks in one service.

connectedFlow.title: Connected learning and operations
connectedFlow.description: Self-study, course-material generation, and participant and class management are available in one web application.

reusableMaterials.title: Reusable course materials
reusableMaterials.description: Generated course materials are stored as data and available as PDFs, allowing staff-prepared content to be used again.

operationalWorkspace.title: Consolidated administration
operationalWorkspace.description: User, staff, course, and session-room management are collected in one workspace for program operations.

walkthrough.title: Product walkthrough
walkthrough.description: The video demonstrates the implemented AI-assisted math and reading activity flow.
